quotes.text: If [your Radar plan](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works.md#compare-plans) supports this feature, card payments that have an elevated risk of fraud are automatically placed into [review](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/transaction-reviews.md).
However, the existence of several of these indicators at the same time can suggest that a payment is fraudulent.
Although a difference in address by itself doesn’t indicate fraud (for example, the customer might have purchased a gift), it indicates that the charge should be looked at more carefully.
If this scenario appears, it might be prudent to refund the entire donation.
You can mark a payment as fraudulent using either the Stripe API or the Dashboard.

old_evidence.text: With _Radar_ (Stripe Radar helps detect and block fraud for any type of business using machine learning that trains on data across millions of global companies. It’s built into Stripe and requires no additional setup to get started) for Fraud Teams, card payments that have an elevated risk of fraud are automatically placed into [review](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews.md).
If this scenario appears, it may be prudent to refund the entire donation.
You can mark a payment as fraudulent using either the Stripe API or the Dashboard.

findings: New raw line 11 changes automatic elevated-risk review from the old explicit Radar for Fraud Teams wording at line 10 to a plan-feature condition, with current transaction-reviews and compare-plans links. The existing source does not discuss this condition; a concise qualified update would preserve the material change without implying all Radar plans provide automatic review.

New raw line 69 and old raw line 68 both frame refunding the entire mistaken large donation as a prudent option. Current source line 45 states an imperative 'refund the entire donation instead'; concept wiki/concepts/disputes.md line 52 states the same imperative. Qualify both as case-specific advice, not an automatic rule.

New raw line 75 and old raw line 74 only state that API or Dashboard can mark a payment fraudulent and link to risk evaluation guidance. Current source line 50 supplies a Dashboard navigation path and API field not evidenced by either capture of this URL. Those details require separate support or a source-level reduction to the claim this URL actually makes.

Core fraud indicators, shipping checks, digital-goods cues, donation scenario, and card-testing advice persist. Most other diff lines are wording, capitalization, and outbound-link destinations; no omission demonstrates deprecation.
substantive_changes: Automatic review eligibility is now expressed as conditional on the Radar plan supporting the feature (new line 11 versus old line 10), rather than named Radar for Fraud Teams.
Reference links for review, risk evaluations, freight forwarding, postal map, and CAPTCHA were updated; destination changes should be kept distinct from feature behavior.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Multiple implicit indicators together can suggest fraud, while individual indicators need not establish it (old line 8; new line 9).
Different shipping and billing addresses alone do not indicate fraud (old line 39; new line 40).
Refunding the entire donation in the stated partial-refund scenario is a prudential option, not a mandatory response (old line 68; new line 69).
Shipping information can improve fraud detection but is not necessary to accept a payment (old line 52; new line 53).
conflicts: Current source line 45 and concept wiki/concepts/disputes.md line 52 overstate the donation advice compared with both captures.
Current source line 50 gives exact Dashboard/API steps that neither captured version of this URL contains; this is an evidence-attribution mismatch rather than proof those steps are false.
unresolved_questions: Whether a separate pinned Stripe source supports the current source line 50 Dashboard path and fraud_details field; this URL alone does not verify those implementation details.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention/identifying-fraud, the material change is the automatic elevated-risk review condition: old raw line 10 names Radar for Fraud Teams, while new raw line 11 says the Radar plan must support the feature. [[source-stripe-disputes-identifying-fraud]] should describe this as conditional, while retaining the stable indicator, shipping, digital-goods, and donation guidance without implying automatic review for every plan.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention/identifying-fraud, old raw line 68 and new raw line 69 both present a full refund after a suspect mistaken donation as something that may or might be prudent. [[source-stripe-disputes-identifying-fraud]] line 45 and [[disputes]] line 52 currently make it an instruction; both need qualification. Old raw line 74 and new raw line 75 support marking fraud through the API or Dashboard, but not the specific implementation steps at source line 50.
